page: Amazon Web Services m8i-flex.4xlarge is a general-purpose instance powered by an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor built on the x86_64 architecture. It features 16 vCPUs (8 physical cores with hyper-threading) running at a clock speed of 3.9 GHz, backed by a 480 MB L3 cache. The instance is equipped with 64.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 7 GHz, yielding a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. It runs on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. There is no local storage or GPU hardware bundled with this instance type, and baseline network bandwidth is rated at 4 Gbps.

Benchmark results indicate strong single-threaded performance, with Geekbench single-core scores and single-threaded compression tasks (such as gzip and bzip3) placing in the top 25% tier. Text processing performance is particularly notable, scoring in the top 10% tier. Multi-core compute, memory bandwidth, and database operations fall within the average range (middle 50%). For machine learning workloads, the CPU's Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) support enables top-tier text generation speeds for small LLM models (135M), though medium model (7B) inference speeds remain average.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the m8i-flex.4xlarge offers a balanced resource density for general-purpose workloads that require modern DDR5 memory speeds and dedicated CPU allocation without the premium cost of local NVMe storage. The primary tradeoff is the lack of local storage and a relatively low baseline network bandwidth of 4 Gbps, which may limit high-throughput data transfer tasks. This instance is suited for text processing, web serving, software compilation, and lightweight machine learning inference.
